source.title: SAUL: Sharpness-Aware Augmented-Lagrangian Unlearning
source.authors: Jaewan Choi; Junyoung Yang; Sangdon Park

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates paraphrased prompts after unlearning: recovery is substantial for Relearning-resilient, partial for its ALM variant, and limited for SAUL and several other methods. This refines the scope of the recovery claim.
record.gate_note: The paraphrased-question evaluation in Tables 1–2 bears on prompting-only recovery. WMDP accuracy and MMLU utility in Table 3 bear on the unlearning-and-utility portion of A. Results cited from other work and hyperparameter-selection values are not recorded. BLUR and PDU have no reported paraphrased-question scores in Table 2.
record.test_reason: The paper runs a prompting-only recovery test: one GPT paraphrase per ToFU forget question, with hyperparameters fixed on the original questions. It applies this to eleven unlearned variants of Llama-3.2-1B at 1%, 5% and 10% forget ratios (Tables 2, 17 and 19); BLUR and PDU have no paraphrase scores. Recovery depends on the method. Relearning-resilient (Fan et al. 2025, a method built to resist relearning) returns to the original model's paraphrased-question level (FROUGE 0.44 vs 0.44, GPT Forget 49.0 vs 50.0). SAUL and most other methods stay near zero. SAUL's WMDP Bio/Cyber accuracy and MMLU on Zephyr-7B-β bear on the efficacy-and-utility part of A, and so do the MUSE tables. None of the originals is this paper.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAUL improves the forgetting–utility trade-off on ToFU, WMDP and MUSE Books under matched forgetting criteria, and that the ALM controller works as a drop-in modifier for other methods. They say SAUL remains effective under ToFU paraphrasing and that the trend holds in Appendix D. However, no paraphrase table for the 3B backbone appears there. They disclaim guarantees against stronger prompting, relearning or recovery attacks. They also note that weight-space SAM robustness does not by itself imply resistance to prompt or recovery attacks. They do not comment on Relearning-resilient's recovery under paraphrase.
record.recipe_differences: SAUL combines a forget-side augmented-Lagrangian constraint, sharpness-aware updates, and separate optimizer states; it does not reproduce the recovery attacks in the named original sources. It tests paraphrased prompts as one limited robustness evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Query rephrasing changes some ToFU results substantially: Relearning-resilient returns close to Original Model scores, while SAUL's GPT-based Forget score remains low. The paper also evaluates multiple methods and forget ratios, but this record focuses on the main 1% paraphrase comparison.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The recovery evaluation covers paraphrased ToFU questions only. The paper explicitly notes that it does not provide formal guarantees against all adversarial prompting, relearning, or recovery attacks. MUSE Books results are from a single run.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 and Table 2 also report utility metrics and other forget ratios; those are not direct recovery measures for the versions cataloged here. BLUR and PDU lack reported paraphrased-question scores in Table 2.

untested.parts: Robustness to fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, jailbreaks or other languages. No attack is run on the WMDP or MUSE models; the only attack is a single GPT paraphrase per ToFU question.
The whole version: no relearning or fine-tuning attack is run.
The whole version: no activation-direction ablation and no analysis of access-blocking versus deletion.
Jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information. Paraphrasing on WMDP or MUSE, or on the Llama-3.2-3B backbone. Only one GPT paraphrase per ToFU question is tested.

Resistance of SAUL and of Relearning-resilient to relearning, internal edits and quantization. Paraphrase robustness on WMDP or MUSE. The authors say weight-space SAM robustness does not by itself imply resistance to prompt or recovery attacks.

missing.what: Paraphrase results at the 5% forget ratio, compared with original-question results. Relearning-resilient: GPT Forget 14.90→61.10 (reference 61.5) and FROUGE 0.01→0.46 (reference 0.45); its MU on original questions is 0.02, a degenerate utility. Relearning-resilient + ALM: GPT Forget 2.40→59.00 and FROUGE 0.01→0.43. Sharp Min–Max: 0.40→3.40. Sharp Min–Max + ALM: 0.70→4.30. SAUL: 0.12→1.10.

Paraphrase results at the 10% forget ratio. Relearning-resilient is only partly unlearned on original questions (GPT Forget 28.75 vs reference 84.5; MU 0.15). Paraphrased, its GPT Forget is 27.00 (reference 67.0), but FROUGE rises 0.01→0.28 (reference 0.48). Relearning-resilient + ALM: GPT 0.92→1.25, FROUGE 0.01→0.03, so no recovery here. Sharp Min–Max + ALM: FROUGE 0.01→0.13. SAUL: GPT 0.30→1.48. SAUL w/o SAM: GPT 0.60→3.60 ± 4.87.

WMDP results for the other methods, plus the corrected Original row (Bio 0.637, Cyber 0.440, MMLU 0.581). Sharp Min–Max: Bio 0.260, Cyber 0.260, MMLU 0.535. Relearning-resilient: 0.262/0.262, MMLU 0.414. BLUR: 0.262/0.253, MMLU 0.540. All were tuned to near chance; Relearning-resilient pays a large utility cost.

MUSE forget and retain results with no attack. Books (single run): Original KnowMem Df 59.4 and Dr 66.9; Retrain 28.9 and 74.5. SAUL: Df 0.77, Dr 48.25. The other methods have Dr 39.03–48.40. News (3 seeds): Original Df 63.9 and Dr 55.2; Retrain 33.1 and 55.0. The methods reach Df 30.8–32.6 with Dr 25.25–31.02. SAUL's News VerbMem is 9.08, against ≤0.73 for the others.

BLUR matches its reported ToFU Forget Quality but still leaks forget-set answers. At 1% it has FROUGE 0.28 and GPT Forget 36.0, against the original model's 82.5. Whether forgetting looks achieved depends on the metric.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:

(1) Split the refused "r1–r44" item into one item per row. All 47 rows now have an item. Record versions are relabelled by what each row measures: V1→A (WMDP/MMLU rows), V5→E (ToFU paraphrase rows and their original-question comparators), V6→F (SAUL paraphrase rows).

(2) Value fixes found in the text:
- r2: Single AdamW's original-question GPT Forget is 0.17 ± 0.08.
- r32: SAUL's paraphrased GPT Forget is 1.50 ± 1.37.
- r36: SAUL w/o ALM is 1.00 ± 2.24.
- r46/r47: the record swapped the Original's Cyber and MMLU baselines. They are Cyber 0.440 and MMLU 0.581, matching Zephyr-7B's published WMDP values. The earlier verdict had accepted an anomalous MMLU of 0.440. SAUL's MMLU is therefore a 3.9-point drop.

(3) For consistency, A is now linked to every paraphrase row, not just six. A new A 'supports' label covers the methods that resist paraphrase. Where a row is linked to E together with A or F, its state is for E (recovery), and the problem text gives the inverse reading for A/F.

(4) F is now linked to the Relearning-resilient rows (r21–r28), with a new F limits_scope label. The paper describes Fan et al. 2025 as a method built to resist relearning, and paraphrase undoes it.

(5) Added two text-based A limits_scope labels with no rows: Relearning-resilient's WMDP MMLU cost, and the retain-knowledge cost on MUSE.

(6) Corrected the 10% missing item. Relearning-resilient was partly unlearned (28.75/84.5), and its FROUGE does rise under paraphrase (0.01→0.28). Added a missing item on BLUR's answer-level leakage.

(7) Fixed 'nine' to 'eleven' variants in test_reason. Kept tranche T2.

Caveats: the WMDP and ToFU forget values on original questions are tuning targets (matched forgetting), not outcomes. Relearning-resilient's ToFU MU collapses at 5% and 10% (0.02, 0.15). The paper says paraphrase results for larger backbones are in Appendix D, but the 3B tables (20–22) cover original questions only and omit Relearning-resilient. No instructions were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The WMDP results test near-chance targeted accuracy and utility preservation, but the full version is not tested as a general claim across methods. Recovery resistance is tested only for query paraphrasing, not fine-tuning, activation edits, or quantization.
No small-set relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack is run.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing access-blocking versus deletion is reported.
No low-bit quantization attack is reported.
Only GPT-paraphrased ToFU questions are evaluated. Jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information are not tested.
SAUL is evaluated against query rephrasing only; resistance to fine-tuning, activation edits, and quantization is not tested.
